page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the arm64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz, with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 192 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is average, and the Geekbench single-core score is weak. However, multi-core execution is strong, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 87,022.37. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only small block cached memory reaching 3,391.09 GB/sec and large block uncached memory write speeds at 78.56 GB/sec. The instance exhibits strong performance in Redis SET operations, processing 61.65 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is average at 34.9 GB/sec.

Tradeoffs are evident in single-threaded tasks and specific workloads. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing are weak, and text generation using a small 135M LLM model is poor at 19.46 tokens per second. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPU acceleration further limits its suitability for heavy storage-bound or deep learning training tasks. This instance is best suited for scale-out workloads that leverage multi-threaded ARM architectures, such as web serving, database operations, software compilation, and general-purpose containerized applications.
